No earlier submissions or grades were supplied.\n\nq-74964: Along y=x, the expression becomes 2x/(2x-1), whose limit is 0. Along y=x^2, it equals 2. Thus I and II are true, and III is false because the two-variable limit does not exist.\nq-142950: P(X=2)=0.6, so the conditional probabilities for Y=2 and Y=4 are 0.2/0.6=1/3 and 0.4/0.6=2/3. MA's final table is correct. Its intermediate equations incorrectly label these as P(X=2|Y=2) and P(X=2|Y=4); those probabilities actually equal 2/3 and 4/7, respectively. Its opening reference to f_{X|Y} also conflicts with the displayed definition of f_{Y|X}.\nq-42579: Expansion along the third row gives det(A)=6(0)-(-3)(-2)=-6, so det(A^{-1})=-1/6.\nq-32649: Using the standard unit-diagonal L convention, the elimination multipliers are l_{21}=1 and l_{32}=-1. The final pivot is u_{33}=7, giving -7.\nq-131502: Negating row 1 and eliminating rows 2 and 3 gives the echelon matrix with first row (1,-3,2,-1) and two zero rows. Thus x=3y-2z-1, with y and z arbitrary real numbers.\nq-42956: Expansion along column 4, then column 3 of the remaining minor, gives 4((-2)(-1)-0)=8.\nq-77433: B-A=(2,-2,2), so the selected line starts at A and has this direction vector.\nq-73551: Divide row 1 by 5, subtract twice row 1 from row 2, then divide row 2 by 2. The resulting rows are (1,-3,2) and (0,1,0).\nq-80657: Linearity and additivity give 4(-5+7)=8.\nq-127727: The speed is e^t. Arc length measured from t=0 is s=e^t-1, so t=ln(s+1). Substitution gives the selected parametrization, with s≥0.\nq-335280: T(t)=20-12e^{-kt}, with k=ln(3/2)/5. Reaching 16 degrees requires t=5ln(3)/ln(3/2)≈13.547 minutes, rounded to 14 minutes.\nq-86590: Removing 2, 6, and 10 from U leaves {4,8,12}.\nq-88830: There are 5 chess-club members among 40 students, giving 1/8.\nq-88892: There are 7 spam emails among 42 emails, giving 1/6.\nq-89031: Total probability gives (9/10)(1/10)+(1/10)(9/10)=9/50.\nq-89041: The weighted probability is (0.23)(0.43)+(0.19)(0.57)=0.2072, which rounds to the offered answer 0.207.",
